claims.claim: Counts may be truncated to {0,1,2} without losing any information relevant to level-3 restoration.
claims.evidence: For h(r)=min(2,r), h(a+b)=h(h(a)+h(b)) and h(ab)=h(h(a)h(b)) for all nonnegative integers. Hence every path count computed using addition and multiplication is preserved as zero, one, or at least two. Each uniqueness quantifier depends only on whether its count is exactly one, so applying a fresh saturated-count lift at the next quantifier loses no relevant information.
claims.witness: The three saturated values distinguish exactly the predicates count=0, count=1, and count>=2. The checker also tested both homomorphism identities for every a,b in 0..40.
claims.search_method: Algebraic case analysis on the saturation map, followed by exact finite checks.

claims.claim: Level-3 additive restoration is decidable in O(m n^3) time under the source paper’s complexity convention.
claims.evidence: For fixed local type-3 and type-2 digits, the 2-by-2 matrix A_i counts type-1 fillings by carry transition. Starting at q_0=(1,0), saturated matrix multiplication therefore counts all type-1 prefixes, and q_m(alpha)=1 is equivalent to a unique valid global type-1 assignment. The second lift counts type-2 prefixes over the nine possible q-states; summing final multiplicities over q with q(alpha)=1 tests the type-2 uniqueness quantifier. The remaining type-3 choices form ordinary layered reachability. Carry states, the nine q-states, and the 3^9 lifted states are constants. Across a column there are only three cells, so enumerating all local type-1, type-2, and type-3 digit tuples costs at most n^3; over m columns the source convention gives O(m n^3).
claims.witness: Every complete digit assignment has one induced carry sequence, so the matrix products neither omit nor duplicate assignments. Exhaustive comparison with direct nested-quantifier evaluation passed all 31,250 two-column base-2 instances, including both possible final carries.
claims.search_method: Re-derived both counting lifts from the source quantifier order, checked boundary carries, analyzed tuple enumeration, and exhaustively compared against direct semantics.

claims.claim: Level-3 additive restoration is exactly a constant-state relational word problem after per-column normalization.
claims.evidence: For each fixed local type-3 assignment x_i, the lifted update d_i=d_{i-1}B_i(x_i) is deterministic on S={0,1,2}^9. Thus a global type-3 assignment induces an R_1...R_m path. Conversely, choosing a witness x_i for each edge gives a consistent global type-3 assignment because restoration cells in distinct columns are distinct. The endpoint condition is precisely that exactly one type-2 assignment has exactly one type-1 completion with final carry alpha. These two directions establish equivalence, not merely a relaxation.
claims.witness: S has 3^9 states; the initial state is the unit mass at q=(1,0), and acceptance is saturated sum_{q:q(alpha)=1} d(q)=1.
claims.search_method: Constructed the forward assignment-to-path map and the reverse edge-witness-to-assignment map, including empty type blocks and final-carry acceptance.

claims.claim: The same construction places every fixed-level additive restoration problem in P.
claims.evidence: Inductively, eliminating one globally unique assignment block from an N-state column automaton replaces its state by a vector in {0,1,2}^N, giving 3^N states and preserving exact-one semantics. Starting from two carry states and repeating for the k-1 unique blocks produces a finite state set depending only on fixed k. The outer type-k existential block is then layered reachability. Local transition construction remains polynomial because a column has only three cells. Empty variable blocks contribute their single empty assignment and require no separate case.
claims.witness: With N_0=2 and N_{j+1}=3^{N_j}, every N_j is constant for fixed j; only the number of columns and local digit enumeration vary with the input.
claims.search_method: Induction on the number of nested uniqueness quantifiers and explicit examination of absent-type cases.

claims.claim: Under the source paper’s polynomial-base convention and any uniform-AC0-decodable explicit-column encoding, every fixed-level additive restoration problem is in logspace-uniform NC1.
claims.evidence: For fixed k the lifted state set is constant. Under n<=N^O(1), all candidate local digit tuples and the pairs needed to recognize a saturated count of at least two can be enumerated by polynomial-size circuits. Fixed-width digit bounds, equality, and two-addend binary addition have uniform-AC0 circuits, while the stated decoder exposes the relevant column fields in uniform AC0. Consequently every constant-dimensional relation R_i is computable in uniform AC0. A balanced tree of Boolean products of these constant-dimensional matrices has polynomial size and O(log m)<=O(log N) depth, and its wiring is generable with logarithmic workspace.
claims.witness: An R_i entry is a fixed-depth Boolean combination of guarded candidate witnesses. Each relation-product entry is an OR of a constant number of ANDs, so each level of the balanced product tree has constant depth.
claims.search_method: Audited leaf-relation size and depth, saturation predicates, binary arithmetic, matrix-product depth, and logspace uniformity under the claim’s explicit encoding qualifications.

claims.claim: Under the source paper’s polynomial encoding convention, every fixed-level additive restoration problem is decidable in deterministic logarithmic space; for every fixed base it is a regular column language.
claims.evidence: For fixed k, the reachable-state bitset and all lifted transition tables have constant size. Processing one explicit column requires only a column-position counter and at most three digit counters, using O(log m+log n) space. The stipulated polynomial-base convention gives log n=O(log N), so total workspace is O(log N). For fixed n and k, cell descriptors form a finite column alphabet, the reachable-state update is finite, and the boundary/final-carry information can be incorporated into finitely many states; hence the normalized column language is regular.
claims.witness: The machine can rescan a column for each constant-state transition and saturate counts immediately, so it never stores an assignment table or a number larger than n.
claims.search_method: Workspace accounting for the streaming lifted automaton, followed by a finite-alphabet DFA construction for fixed base and level.

claims.claim: Level-3 additive restoration is formally P-complete under polynomial-time many-one reductions, but this does not provide the requested meaningful matching hardness classification.
claims.evidence: Membership in P follows from the verified algorithm. The language has fixed YES and NO instances. For any L in P, a polynomial-time reduction may decide its input and output the fixed YES instance or fixed NO instance accordingly, proving hardness under polynomial-time many-one reductions. This argument applies to every nontrivial P language and supplies no hardness under a weaker, discriminating reduction, so the draft correctly refuses to treat it as the requested matching classification.
claims.witness: In base 2 with final carry 0, the one-column instance T3+0=0 is YES, while T3+1=0 is NO. Both were checked directly and through the lifted recurrence.
claims.search_method: Applied the definition of polynomial-time many-one hardness and independently verified the two fixed instances.

claims.claim: Even in base 2 with no type-3 cells, level-3 additive restoration is ODD-PARITY-hard under constant-length projections, and therefore is not in AC0.
claims.evidence: For U=(T1,T1,T1), direct column counting gives [[2,1],[1,2]], while I=(0,1,T1) is the identity. After the U prefix the state is E=(2,1). Across VU, where V=(0,1,T2), digit 0 maps E to O=(1,2) and digit 1 maps E to M=(2,2); from O only digit 1 returns to E, and every other choice enters absorbing M. Thus exactly one type-2 assignment avoids M, and it ends at O exactly when the input has odd parity. With final carry 0, only O has count one. The empty type-3 block leaves this truth value unchanged. Replacing each bit by its fixed two-column block is a constant-length projection, so closure of AC0 under projections and the parity lower bound exclude AC0.
claims.witness: Exact transition table: (E,0)->O, (E,1)->M, (O,0)->M, (O,1)->E, and (M,c)->M. Direct and lifted evaluation matched odd parity for all 31 words of lengths 0 through 4.
claims.search_method: Derived all gadget matrices from the base-2 column equation, proved the E/O/M invariant by induction, and checked bounded words exactly.

claims.claim: The meaningful classification is narrowed to a projection lower bound by ODD PARITY and a deterministic-logspace upper bound, but no matching hardness classification is established.
claims.evidence: Claims 5 and 7 establish the stated substantive bracket under the source convention. Parity hardness only excludes AC0 and does not establish L-hardness or P-hardness under an appropriately weak reduction. The draft supplies no matching reduction. Its observation that logspace-reduction P-hardness together with membership in L would imply P=L is correct but is only an obstruction, not a hardness result.
claims.witness: The established implications are ODD-PARITY <=projection Level-3-Additive-Restoration and Level-3-Additive-Restoration in L.
claims.search_method: Checked both endpoint proofs and searched the supplied draft for a reduction establishing hardness matching the L upper bound; none is present.

claims.claim: For uniform-AC0-decodable explicit-column encodings, the meaningful classification is narrowed to a projection lower bound by ODD PARITY and a logspace-uniform NC1 upper bound, but no matching hardness classification is established.
claims.evidence: Under the stated explicit-column encoding qualification, claim 4 gives the logspace-uniform NC1 upper bound, while the fixed base-2 column substitution in claim 7 gives the projection lower bound. Parity is not NC1-complete under the relevant weak reductions, and the draft supplies no reduction from an NC1-complete language. The endpoints therefore do not match, exactly as claimed.
claims.witness: The proven bracket is ODD-PARITY <=projection Level-3-Additive-Restoration in logspace-uniform NC1, with strictness neither asserted nor proved.
claims.search_method: Combined the independently checked conditional circuit construction with the exact parity gadget and inspected whether any matching NC1-hardness argument was supplied.

target_evidence: The draft gives a complete decision procedure for level 3, extends the upper bound to every fixed level, and proves a nontrivial parity projection lower bound. It does not establish hardness matching either the deterministic-logspace or encoding-qualified logspace-uniform-NC1 upper bound. Formal P-completeness under polynomial-time reductions is nondiscriminating because the reduction may decide its source language. Therefore the requested matching hardness classification remains unresolved, and the draft’s PARTIAL resolution claim is accurate.
checks_performed: Verified all ten supplied claim SHA-256 bindings against the parent claim strings.
Read only /evidence/source.json and /evidence/parent.json; used no web or other evidence, solution, receipt, database, arm, or prior-run file.
Re-derived the saturated semiring recurrence, both uniqueness lifts, final-carry condition, and outer existential relation from the source definitions.

The checker passed saturation identities, the fixed YES/NO instances, all E/O/M gadget transitions, exhaustive direct-versus-lifted evaluation of 31,250 two-column base-2 instances, and all parity words of lengths 0 through 4.
Audited the O(m n^3), deterministic-logspace, regular-language, and encoding-qualified logspace-uniform-NC1 bounds separately from the finite checks.
Confirmed that no matching L-hardness or NC1-hardness reduction is established, so the source target is only partially resolved.
